title: US Stock Futures Dip Before Nvidia, Oil Declines: Markets Wrap

title: Short Squeeze in US Long Bonds Shows ‘Bessent Put’ at Work
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s surprise plan to tamp down US borrowing costs by expanding bond buybacks may have sparked fierce debate about its ultimate effectiveness, but key market metrics and positioning show that it’s having an impact.

title: Citadel Securities’ Flight Reverses Bearish Call on Long Bonds
summary: Citadel Securities’ Frank Flight, who just last month warned of  a “cruel summer” for US bond investors, now sees the balance of risks tilted toward a rally, citing crowded bearish positioning and improving inflation data.

title: Xi Signals Defiance as US Threatens Sanctions Over Iran
summary: Xi Jinping’s government is sending a message of defiance to Donald Trump over China’s economic ties with Iran. Bloomberg's Michael Heath breaks down the options available to Donald Trump to strangle Iran's economy and end a conflict that's pulling US resources from Asia. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: China Banks Use Overnight Rate for Bonds as PBOC Reform Widens
summary: Chinese lenders have started pricing bonds off the nation’s overnight funding cost, an indication that it’s increasingly the benchmark for the financial system.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 26
summary: Oil fell for a third day as Iran and Oman discussed an “interim framework” aimed at resuming shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Gold Holds Five-Day Gain as Oil Drop Eases Inflation Concerns
summary: Gold held a five-day gain, with inflation concerns eased by a drop in US Treasury yields and lower oil prices as Iran and Oman discussed ways to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Record Short Bets Hit China’s AI Model Duo on Fierce Competition
summary: Bearish bets against shares of Z.AI Co. and MiniMax Group Inc. have soared to records ahead of their earnings reports, highlighting growing investor worry over China’s heated AI rivalry.

title: Xi’s Unprecedented Tax Clawback Hammers Chinese Listed Companies
summary: During more than two decades as a public company, Heilongjiang Agriculture Co. never once reported a first-half loss. That run is ending this year.

title: Fusion Firm Gets Major Monetary Boost
summary: Commonwealth Fusion Systems has raised around $4 billion in order to work toward commercializing fusion energy, that's about 30% of the total capital raised by the fusion industry to-date, according to CFS. In explaining on Bloomberg Businessweek what fusion is, the company's CEO Bob Mumgaard says the goal "is to build a machine that can make this reaction go at very vigorous amounts of energy at an industrial scale." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gold Edges Up After Four-Day Gain as Traders Eye Treasury Moves
summary: Gold edged higher as inflation concerns eased, extending a four-day rally sparked by a surprise bond-market intervention that’s revived concerns over US fiscal policy and dollar weakness.

title: 2026 Best Cities for Work Revealed
summary: Indeed Hiring Lab measured 40 metrics across six pillars against hundreds of US metro-areas to determine which cities are the best for workers in 2026. Laura Ullrich, Director of Economic Research at Indeed Hiring Lab, explains that its not about where company's are headquartered or where its best to run a company, but where Indeed is seeing the most career dynamism and opportunity -- so the top cities for workers may surprise you. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How LeBron James Scored $300 Million From Insurers
summary: When LeBron James signed up to lead the Los Angeles Lakers to NBA glory with a $154 million contract in 2018, it wasn’t the biggest deal he did that year. His limited liability company borrowed almost $300 million from two Midwestern life insurers, Sridhar Natarajan explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Northrop CEO on Defense Spending, Golden Dome System
summary: Northrop Grumman Chair, CEO and President Kathy Warden discusses doing business with the Trump administration, working on the Golden Dome space defense system and how geopolitical tensions and active conflicts are fueling a global defense spending boom. She speaks with Bloomberg's Kailey Leinz at a Newsmakers event in Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Conference Board CEO: Consumers Worried About the Future
summary: Steve Odland, CEO of The Conference Board, discussed the recent consumer confidence data showing a significant divergence between current sentiment and future expectations. The present situation index increased by 6.8 points, reflecting consumers' relatively positive feelings due to full employment and rising wages. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Emily Graffeo on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The Mormon Church Is Putting Its Real Estate Empire to Work
summary: After decades of quietly amassing billions of dollars in land, the institution is investing in more deals and planning massive projects that stand to reshape communities. Bloomberg's Natalie Wong, Ann Choi and Katie Meyer explain. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: EchoStar Deals Worth $1.5 Billion Must be Investigated, US Says
summary: EchoStar Corp. allegedly engaged in $1.5 billion of “unusual transactions” with its bankrupt subsidiary, Hughes Satellite Systems Corp., according to the US Trustee, who urged the court to appoint an examiner to investigate the deals.

title: Stocks Rise Before Nvidia as Oil Drop Lifts Bonds: Markets Wrap
summary: Stocks rose as a decline in oil prices sent bond yields lower, with traders awaiting Nvidia Corp.’s earnings for clues on whether the outlook for artificial intelligence remains intact.

title: Intuit Sinks 11% on Weak Outlook as Nvidia Earnings Loom | Closing Bell
summary: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Emily Graffeo, Norah Mulinda and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Oil Falls on Fresh Iran War Diplomacy, Talks on Hormuz
summary: Oil extended declines as fresh diplomatic efforts helped renew optimism the Iran war would not escalate, while a US plan to ramp up economic pressure on Tehran spared the country’s trading partners from harsher measures for now.
